_comment: Mode A/C pre-filter applied by every volunteer's client before sending. Edit and save: mlat-server re-reads this within 15 s and pushes it to all connected clients. A file with a mistake is ignored (the current settings stay) and the reason is in: docker compose logs mlat-server

mode_a_match._comment: Drop a code that is the squawk of a Mode S / ADS-B aircraft the receiver heard in the last window_s seconds. Codes in never_drop are always sent: several aircraft can share them.

mode_c_match._comment: Drop a code that is the Mode C altitude (+/- tolerance_ft) of a Mode S / ADS-B aircraft the receiver heard in the last window_s seconds. Off: airliners fill most flight levels, so this would also drop unknown aircraft's altitude replies.

reply_pairing._comment: Link a squawk and an altitude code of the same aircraft at each receiver, two ways: sandwich = squawk, altitude, squawk at the radar's exact interrogation spacing and the same signal level (fast); correlation = the two codes heard in the same beam dwells at the same mean signal level, dwell after dwell (slower; also works on radars with staggered timing; OFF because on real traffic it linked airliners at different flight levels: 41 right / 108 wrong, against sandwich 23 / 0). Links obey real-aircraft rules: two squawks never link, and a discrete squawk keeps only its strongest altitude. drop_paired: drop an altitude reply whose every partner is a dropped code (known Mode S traffic, 1200 VFR) - an unknown on 4000 keeps its altitude. send_hints: tell ac-filter about unknowns' squawk/altitude links so it pairs them at once. The rest is tuning: try values with tools/ac_capture.py on a recording first.
